[
  {"sentence": 1, "status": "present", "evidence": "Prologue: on the sinking Lusitania a frightened man hands an American girl an oilskin packet of 'vitally important papers' because of 'women and children first.' Carter later names him as Danvers and her as Jane Finn.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 2, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Tommy, old thing!' 'Tuppence, old bean!' Tommy is demobbed; Tuppence is the 'fifth daughter of Archdeacon Cowley' and did hospital work.", "note": "The abridgment implies the postwar timing rather than stating 'four years later'."},
  {"sentence": 3, "status": "present", "evidence": "Both are 'stony' and jobless. 'The Young Adventurers, Ltd.!' and an advertisement offering 'Two young adventurers for hire.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 4, "status": "present", "evidence": "Whittington: 'I happened to overhear part of your conversation.' He offers £100 to enter 'Madame Colombier's' pensionnat in Paris.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 5, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Jane Finn,' she said hastily... Whittington 'purple with rage.' 'Here's fifty to go on with.' Next day the office is closed down and the company 'left rather suddenly.' Tommy overheard the name in the street.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 6, "status": "present", "evidence": "'WANTED, any information respecting Jane Finn.' ... 'there are only two answers!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 7, "status": "present", "evidence": "The first letter is signed 'A. CARTER.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 8, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Yes, sir, I recognized you at once. Saw you in France when I was with the Intelligence.' Tommy later says 'he's IT!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 9, "status": "present", "evidence": "Carter describes the draft secret agreement Danvers carried. The girl 'never arrived'. The treaty 'implicates a number of our statesmen'. 'Bolshevist gold is pouring into this country to procure a Revolution.' The strike menace is planned.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 10, "status": "present", "evidence": "The man behind the Bolshevists is 'always spoken of by the unassuming title of \"Mr. Brown.\"'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 11, "status": "present", "evidence": "'a certain man, whose real name is unknown to us'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 12, "status": "present", "evidence": "'How would you like to work for me?... Find Jane Finn.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 13, "status": "present", "evidence": "The second letter is from the Ritz, signed 'JULIUS P. HERSHEIMMER.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 14, "status": "present", "evidence": "Julius says Jane is his cousin. 'Inspector Brown' took 'the only copy in existence' of her photograph, and this led to a 'rapprochement' with the Young Adventurers.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 15, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tuppence reasons that Danvers was shadowed, probably by a woman who may have been 'Rita', and they search the list of survivors.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 16, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Mrs. Vandemeyer, 20 South Audley Mansions'... 'Marguerite'... 'She's mostly called that [Rita].'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 17, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tommy follows Boris to a house in Soho, copies the knock and says 'Mr. Brown?', and is sent upstairs.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 18, "status": "present", "evidence": "He overhears the meeting presided over by Number One, later identified as Kramenin. The date given is 'The 29th.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 19, "status": "present", "evidence": "'A crashing blow descended on his head.' He bargains for his life against 'The papers that Danvers brought over.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 20, "status": "present", "evidence": "Albert, the lift-boy, arranges for Tuppence to take Annie's place.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 21, "status": "present", "evidence": "Mrs. Vandemeyer hires 'Prudence Cooper' as house-parlourmaid.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 22, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Sir James Peel Edgerton... the famous K.C.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 23, "status": "present", "evidence": "'a change does no harm sometimes... Just a hint.' He later agrees to help find Tommy.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 24, "status": "present", "evidence": "'a rim of cold steel touched her temple'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 25, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tuppence seizes the revolver ('Now who's on top...') and offers 'a hundred thousand' from an American millionaire for the name of Mr. Brown.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 26, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Who is Mr. Brown?'... 'I'll do it.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 27, "status": "present", "evidence": "She faints on seeing Sir James and Julius in the doorway. They keep a vigil, and by morning she is dead. 'Rather an odour of chloral'; the bottle is empty.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 28, "status": "present", "evidence": "Dr. Hall reveals 'Janet Vandemeyer' was at his Bournemouth home with 'a complete loss of memory' and has since been taken away.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 29, "status": "present", "evidence": "Julius proposes and asks her to think it over. Tuppence says 'I do love you so' to Tommy's photo. Her note reads 'Let's leave it till then.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 30, "status": "present", "evidence": "The telegram signed 'TOMMY' says 'Come at once, Moat House, Ebury, Yorkshire.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 31, "status": "present", "evidence": "Annette slips him a penknife and helps him escape, crying 'To Marguerite!' At the Ritz, Miss Cowley 'had gone out.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 32, "status": "present", "evidence": "A week of searching around Ebury finds only her brooch: 'no nearer to discovering Tuppence's whereabouts.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 33, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Jane Finn found... PEEL EDGERTON.' Her memory is restored, and they follow her directions to the gorse path and the dog-shaped boulder near Holyhead. The packet reveals 'WITH THE COMPLIMENTS OF MR. BROWN.'", "note": "The message appears as sympathetic ink brought out by heat. This is a detail difference, not a material distortion."},
  {"sentence": 34, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tuppence's green toque and a coat are 'washed up on the Yorkshire coast.' Tommy shouts at Julius: 'but I loved her.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 35, "status": "present", "evidence": "He finds Annette's photograph in Julius's writing-table. His letter to Carter says 'that girl at Manchester was just a plant' and 'I think I know who the real Jane Finn is.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 36, "status": "present", "evidence": "'I kept my mind open between the two of them.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 37, "status": "present", "evidence": "He leaves Julius a note about the Argentine and shows Sir James's letter. The altered telegram reveals 'Astley Priors, Gatehouse, Kent.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 38, "status": "present", "evidence": "'She'd never spell her name \"Twopence\"... Julius had seen it... but Sir James hadn't!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 39, "status": "present", "evidence": "Julius makes Kramenin bring out the girls at gunpoint. Jane says 'I guess there's nothing wrong with your memory' and confirms 'Five long years!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 40, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Go straight to Sir James Peel Edgerton.' Jane hid the papers behind the picture 'Marguerite with her casket of jewels' in the Soho room.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 41, "status": "present", "evidence": "Jane extracts the two sheets. Sir James says: 'I am Mr. Brown.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 42, "status": "present", "evidence": "He raises the automatic but is 'seized from behind in a grip of iron' by Julius and Tommy, who had hidden behind the curtain in the recess.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 43, "status": "present", "evidence": "'the hand which bore the big signet ring, was raised to his lips... an odour of bitter almonds'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 44, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Deprived of their chief, the organization fell to pieces.' The treaty was 'reduced to ashes.' 'It was to be Peace, not War!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 45, "status": "present", "evidence": "At the Savoy supper, Carter reads from the brown diary. Sir William says 'Shall we let bygones be bygones... You're my heir.' Jane is toasted as 'one of the bravest of America's daughters!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 46, "status": "present", "evidence": "Julius proposes to Jane, who says 'I love you now, Julius.' In the taxi Tuppence says 'Ours, so there!' and Tommy replies 'You won't be able to get out of marrying me.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 47, "status": "present", "evidence": "'But do you know what I think it is?' 'A sport!' 'And a damned good sport too.' The plucky, commonsense pair defeat Mr. Brown.", "note": ""}
]
